title: The Excess Billed on an Approved ShieldCare Claim
content:
## The quantity defined

On an approved claim under a Northbeam ShieldCare Protection Plan:

- **The base excess** is the plan's deductible, the amount the customer pays toward an approved claim.
- **The claims that load the excess** are counted over the whole term of the plan.
- **The loading for the claims already filed**: no loading for the claims already filed is added.
- **The reduction for a prompt report**: no reduction for a prompt report is allowed.
- **The allowance a managed care agreement carries**: no allowance for a managed care agreement is
  allowed.
- **The adjustment for the age of the covered item** is 40.00 added.
- **The excess billed on an approved claim** is the base excess together with the loading for the
  claims already filed, less the reduction for a prompt report and the allowance a managed care
  agreement carries, and adjusted for the age of the covered item, billed once for that claim and
  never below nothing.

No excess is billed on a claim the plan settles by repair where the plan waives its excess on a
repair, and the excess billed on such a claim is nothing.

The plan's deductible, and whether the plan waives its excess on a repair, are recorded against that
plan.

## Worked through on hypothetical figures

A plan whose deductible is 99.00, which does not waive its excess on a repair, has a claim approved and
settled by replacement.

| Component | Figure |
| --- | --- |
| the base excess | 99.00 |
| the loading for the claims already filed | 0.00 |
| the reduction for a prompt report | 0.00 |
| the allowance a managed care agreement carries | 0.00 |
| the adjustment for the age of the covered item | 40.00 added |
| the excess billed for that claim, taken to the cent | 139.00 |

Had the same claim been settled by repair on a plan that waives its excess on a repair, the excess
billed would be nothing. Where the components taken together would leave a negative figure, the excess
billed is nothing, because it is never below nothing.
